key_claims.claim: Sequencing after negative CMA in prenatal ACC yields pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in 30% overall, with 17% yield in isolated ACC and 41% when extracranial anomalies are present.
Size-selective cfDNA enrichment achieves approximately 19% mean fetal fraction and 59% PPV for CNV detection across a large clinical cohort.
After PGT-A euploid transfer, residual confirmed aneuploidy is 0.1%, and cfDNA sensitivity for detecting these cases is only 50% with a PPV of 12.5%.
No single sagittal aortic-arch parameter reliably predicts prenatal coarctation across centers; a multivariable model outperforms individual metrics.
Integrated molecular autopsy combining deep phenotyping with exome or genome sequencing achieves 68% diagnostic yield in consanguineous perinatal cases with severe anomalies.
